prompt.context_jp: 正社員と派遣が同じフロアに交ざって働く景色___、もはや当たり前のものとなっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 正社員と派遣が同じフロアに交ざって働く景色___、もはや当たり前のものとなっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks this scene as the established topic the narrator is commenting on.

feedback.correct_en: The narration takes 'the sight of regulars and temps mingling' as a known theme and comments on it ('has become commonplace'). は marks that topic-plus-commentary structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce this sight as brand-new information being spotted; here the narrator is instead reflecting on a settled fact. を is impossible — 景色 is the subject, not an object.

contrast_examples.jp: この景色は当たり前になった。
contrast_examples.en: This sight has become commonplace. (topic + comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 珍しい景色が目に入った。
contrast_examples.en: An unusual sight caught my eye. (new information)

prompt.context_jp: 現在 派遣人口140万人。しかし 給料___時給制で
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし 給料___時給制で
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that sets up the contrast signaled by しかし.

feedback.correct_en: After しかし ('however'), 給料 is picked out contrastively against the positive-sounding '1.4 million workers' — a classic 'as for pay, though...' use of は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 給料 as newly spotted information rather than something being contrasted with what was just said.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事は多い。しかし給料は低い。
contrast_examples.en: There's lots of work. However, the pay is low. (contrast)
Oh, my pay just came in! (new info)

prompt.context_jp: その環境___不安定で厳しい。
prompt.prompt_jp: その環境___不安定で厳しい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the summarizing narration?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator has just listed the conditions of temp work and now comments on 'that environment' as the established topic. は fits the 'about X, (it) is Y' summary move.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce その環境 as new information, but it was just set up — the sentence is a comment, not a discovery.

contrast_examples.en: This job is tough. (comment on topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 新しい仕事が始まった。
contrast_examples.en: A new job started. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: よかったですね 福岡さん 無遅刻 無欠勤で 真面目に頑張った___ですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 真面目に頑張った___ですよ 契約更新 おめでとう
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies the exact reason the contract was renewed.

feedback.correct_en: The clause gives the reason for the renewal: '(it's) because you worked diligently.' から marks cause here, which the closing ~ですよ confirms as an explanatory 'that's why'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and は would leave the sentence without a reason marker, breaking the 'because... that's why' logic the speaker is building.

contrast_examples.en: It's because you worked hard. (reason)

contrast_examples.jp: 頑張ったのがよかった。
contrast_examples.en: The fact that you worked hard was good. (nominalized subject)

prompt.context_jp: 覚悟してるよ 僕も東海林さんも あの人のおかげで 今___あるんだし
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人のおかげで 今___あるんだし
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that presents 'the present' as what exists thanks to her.

feedback.correct_en: The idiom 今がある ('our present (success) exists') asserts the existence of their current status — が marks the newly asserted existing subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 今は ある would turn 今 into a contrastive topic ('as for now, there is...'), which doesn't match the fixed collocation 今がある. を is wrong because ある isn't transitive here.

contrast_examples.jp: 君のおかげで今がある。
contrast_examples.en: I owe my present to you. (set phrase)
As for now, it's different from before. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 名___大前春子、資格の数だけ肩書きを持つ、伝説の派遣である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 名___大前春子、資格の数だけ肩書きを持つ、伝説の派遣である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits an introduction of the protagonist?

feedback.correct_en: 'As for her name — Omae Haruko' is a textbook X は Y だ identification/topic sentence used to introduce a character.
feedback.incorrect_en: 名が大前春子 would sound like answering 'who among them is Omae Haruko?' — exhaustive listing, which doesn't match this calm introduction.

contrast_examples.en: Her name is Haruko. Her job is temp work. (topic framing)
Haruko is (the one named) Omae. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 曲が途切れると、部屋の窓___はすでに朝の光が差し込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の窓___はすでに朝の光が差し込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks where the morning light reached?

feedback.correct_en: 差し込む takes に to mark the destination/surface the light streams into. The window is the point of arrival of the light.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would frame the window as the location where an activity happens, but light streaming 'into' something is a goal, not a venue. を doesn't fit this intransitive verb's role here.

contrast_examples.en: Light streams in through the window. (point of arrival)
I read a book in the room. (venue of activity)

prompt.context_jp: 新年度の初日、宇野部長___上機嫌で里中の席に立ち寄ってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新年度の初日、宇野部長___上機嫌で里中の席に立ち寄ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Manager Uno as he enters the scene?

feedback.correct_en: Uno hasn't been on-stage; the narrator introduces him as a newly appearing actor doing something. Event-reporting/new-subject が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: 宇野部長は would signal that Uno was already the ongoing topic, but he's just walking into the scene for the first time this chapter.

contrast_examples.en: The manager came in. (new event)
The manager, for his part, was in a good mood. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 今年は営業部の花見 いつ やるんだ？ — 今年の花見___… 若い社員たち 行きたがらないんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 今年の花見___… 若い社員たち 行きたがらないんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'this year's hanami' as the topic Satonaka is responding about?

feedback.correct_en: Satonaka picks up 'this year's hanami' from Uno's question as the topic and comments on it — the classic 'as for X...' use of は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present '今年の花見' as newly-identified information, but it's literally what Uno just asked about — it's already shared ground.

contrast_examples.jp: 今年の花見は難しそうです。
contrast_examples.en: As for this year's hanami, it looks difficult. (topic response)

contrast_examples.jp: 今年の花見が中止になった。
contrast_examples.en: This year's hanami got cancelled. (announcing an event)

prompt.context_jp: この人 本当に お前に社長賞を取らせた 伝説のスーパーハケンな___？
prompt.prompt_jp: この人 本当に お前に社長賞を取らせた 伝説のスーパーハケンな___？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the ending that asks for confirmation in casual speech.

feedback.correct_en: Uno is pressing Satonaka for explanation/confirmation of a surprising fact — casual explanatory の with rising intonation does exactly that.
feedback.incorrect_en: が/は after a なーnoun predicate here don't form a natural question seeking clarification; without の there's no 'is it really the case that...' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: You're really a teacher? (seeking explanation)
Where's the teacher? (plain question)

prompt.context_jp: 課長 ここは派遣___足りません
prompt.prompt_jp: ここは派遣___足りません
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'temps' as the thing that is in short supply?

feedback.correct_en: With 足りない (exist/suffice-type predicate), the thing lacking is marked by が. Omae's blunt announcement 'temps are insufficient' pushes 派遣 as new focal information.
feedback.incorrect_en: 派遣は足りません would contrastively imply 'temps aren't enough (but something else is)', which isn't her point. を doesn't work — 足りない is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: There aren't enough hands. (focus on shortage)

contrast_examples.jp: 人手は足りているが時間がない。
contrast_examples.en: Hands are enough, but there's no time. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 大前さん ロシア語___得意ですよね？
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前さん ロシア語___得意ですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the standard 'good at X' pattern?

feedback.correct_en: With adjectives like 得意/好き/上手, the thing one is good at takes が. Satonaka is highlighting Russian as Omae's specific strength.
feedback.incorrect_en: ロシア語は得意 is possible but would contrast Russian with other languages; here Satonaka isn't contrasting, he's naming her key skill. を is ungrammatical with 得意.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はロシア語が得意だ。
contrast_examples.en: He's good at Russian. (standard pattern)

contrast_examples.jp: 英語は苦手だが、ロシア語は得意だ。
contrast_examples.en: English I'm bad at, but Russian I'm good at. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 社運の懸かった大事な仕事___派遣に任せるなんて おかしいだろ
prompt.prompt_jp: 社運の懸かった大事な仕事___派遣に任せるなんて おかしいだろ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the thing being entrusted?

feedback.correct_en: 任せる takes [thing]を[person]に: 'entrust X to Y.' The important work is the direct object being handed over.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a subject and break the transitive structure. は could topicalize, but the fixed 〜を〜に任せる frame is what the speaker actually uses here.

contrast_examples.en: Entrust the work to a subordinate.
As for the work, I left it to him. (topicalized)

prompt.context_jp: お茶っ葉___いつもと同じなんです でも 入れ方が違うんですよね？
prompt.prompt_jp: お茶っ葉___いつもと同じなんです でも 入れ方が違うんですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets up the 'same leaves, but different brewing' contrast.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence pairs 'お茶っ葉は同じ' vs '入れ方が違う' — classic は...が... contrast where は isolates the leaves as one pole against the brewing method.
feedback.incorrect_en: お茶っ葉が同じ would just report sameness without the 'as for the leaves' contrastive framing that the でも...違う response depends on.

contrast_examples.jp: 味は同じだが見た目が違う。
contrast_examples.en: The taste is the same, but the appearance is different. (は vs が contrast)
I was relieved that the taste was the same. (plain assertion)

prompt.context_jp: それだけ仕事ができたらさ 正社員のねたみ___買ったりしないのかな？
prompt.prompt_jp: 正社員のねたみ___買ったりしないのかな？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes the idiom 'to attract (someone's) envy/anger'?

feedback.correct_en: The set phrase is ねたみを買う ('invite envy') — a 〜を買う idiom like 恨みを買う, 不評を買う. The emotion is the direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: ねたみが買う makes 買う intransitive, breaking the idiom. ねたみに doesn't fit the 〜を買う pattern.

contrast_examples.en: To invite a colleague's resentment. (idiom)
To buy a book. (literal 買う)

prompt.context_jp: 派遣なんか___頼ったりしたから 出世街道 踏み外して
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣なんか___頼ったりしたから 出世街道 踏み外して
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle goes with 頼る ('to rely on')?

feedback.correct_en: 頼る lexically takes に to mark who/what you depend on. Shoji blames his career derailment on relying on a temp.
feedback.incorrect_en: を頼る is a rare literary variant and sounds off in this angry spoken complaint. で would frame the temp as a means in a way 頼る doesn't accept.

contrast_examples.en: To rely on one's parents.
To look it up with a dictionary. (means で)

prompt.context_jp: 俺も やっと運___回ってきたよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺も やっと運___回ってきたよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the happy announcement 'luck has finally come around to me'?

feedback.correct_en: The set phrase 運が回ってくる ('luck comes around') presents 運 as a newly arriving subject — exactly the event-reporting が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 運は回ってくる would sound like a contrast ('as for luck, it does come...'), undercutting the excited announcement. を doesn't fit the intransitive 回ってくる.

contrast_examples.jp: やっとチャンスが来た。
contrast_examples.en: A chance has finally come. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: チャンスはいつでも来る。
contrast_examples.en: Chances come anytime. (generic topic)

prompt.context_jp: 私を雇って ___ はさせません 3か月間 お時給の分は しっかり働かせていただきます
prompt.prompt_jp: 私を雇って ___ はさせません
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word that makes a confident 'you won't regret hiring me' promise.

feedback.correct_en: 後悔はさせません ('I won't let you regret it') is a fixed self-confident promise, exactly Omae's flavor of blunt professional pride.
feedback.incorrect_en: 失望させません exists but isn't the set phrase Omae uses; 心配はさせません ('won't make you worry') would sound personal/reassuring, not confident-defiant.

contrast_examples.en: You won't regret it. (set confident promise)

contrast_examples.jp: ご心配をおかけしません。
contrast_examples.en: I won't cause you worry. (softer, apologetic)

prompt.context_jp: うちも今 彼女のこと ___ 手を尽くして探しております
prompt.prompt_jp: うちも今 彼女のこと ___ 手を尽くして探しております
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'doing everything possible from every angle'?

feedback.correct_en: 八方手を尽くす ('exhaust every direction / leave no stone unturned') is the fixed idiom Kon uses to reassure the client.
feedback.incorrect_en: 四方 and 一方 are real words but don't form this set phrase with 手を尽くす — only 八方 is lexicalized here.

contrast_examples.jp: 八方手を尽くして探す。
contrast_examples.en: Search by every means possible. (set phrase)
Look around in all four directions. (literal)

prompt.context_jp: ___ ってことですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ ってことですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Chiba asks Aki if she's just going to silently endure the harassment. Which phrase means 'suffer in silence'?

feedback.correct_en: 泣き寝入り literally 'crying oneself to sleep' = giving up and letting an injustice slide. Chiba is calling out Aki's passivity.
feedback.incorrect_en: 居眠り is 'dozing off (at your desk)' and 早寝 is 'going to bed early' — neither has the 'swallow the injustice' meaning Chiba needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 被害者が泣き寝入りする。
contrast_examples.en: A victim suffers in silence.
Doze off during class.

prompt.context_jp: それでも今夜だけは、あと三か月ぶんの ___ が彼女の背筋を少しだけ伸ばさせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: あと三か月ぶんの ___ が彼女の背筋を少しだけ伸ばさせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun fits 'the ___ of three more months straightened her back a little'?

feedback.correct_en: The renewal is good news; 安堵 ('relief') is what makes her stand a bit taller. The narration is painting a brief moment of release.
feedback.incorrect_en: 不安 ('anxiety') and 緊張 ('tension') are the opposite feeling — those would hunch her shoulders, not straighten them.

contrast_examples.en: Let out a sigh of relief.
Can't sleep from anxiety.

prompt.context_jp: 安くて おいしいの 栄養の ___ も取れるし
prompt.prompt_jp: 栄養の ___ も取れるし
prompt.prompt_en: Which word collocates with 栄養の〜を取る?

feedback.correct_en: 栄養のバランスを取る ('balance one's nutrition') is the standard collocation — it's what justifies Omae's cheap lunch choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: リズム and コース don't pair with 栄養 in Japanese. バランスを取る is the fixed phrase for nutritional balance.

contrast_examples.jp: 栄養のバランスを取る。
contrast_examples.en: Balance one's nutrition. (set collocation)

contrast_examples.jp: 生活のリズムを整える。
contrast_examples.en: Get one's life rhythm in order. (different collocation)

prompt.context_jp: さっさと仕事に戻りなさい この残業代 ___
prompt.prompt_jp: この残業代 ___
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun does Omae use to scold Chiba for lingering past hours?

feedback.correct_en: 〜泥棒 is a productive insult form: 時間泥棒, 残業代泥棒 = 'someone stealing (paid) overtime by loafing.' It matches Omae's sharp tongue.
feedback.incorrect_en: 詐欺 and 犯人 are related crime vocabulary but don't form a casual compound insult like 〜泥棒 does.

contrast_examples.en: Time thief.
Get scammed. (different frame)

prompt.context_jp: Noon has arrived. Omae stands up abruptly to go to lunch, strictly observing her contract.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most like the curt, contract-citing Omae we see in the show?

choices.text: 12時だからちょっと行きますね
もう12時ですけど、よろしいでしょうか

feedback.correct_en: 〜なので失礼します is clipped, formal, and gives an unarguable reason — it matches Omae's style of leaving zero room for negotiation.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too casual and softening (ちょっと、ね), (c) asks permission, which Omae pointedly does not do. Neither matches her blunt professional register.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間なので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: It's time, so I'll excuse myself. (clipped and firm)

contrast_examples.jp: もう帰ってもいいですか？
contrast_examples.en: May I head home now? (asking permission)

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka reminds Omae they met 13 years ago. Omae brushes it off coolly.
prompt.prompt_en: Which brush-off best matches Omae's cold, formal-but-dismissive style?

choices.text: いちいち正社員の顔と名前など 覚えていられませんが 何か？
正社員の顔や名前、全部覚えるのは無理ですよ〜
ごめんなさい、ちょっと思い出せなくて…

feedback.correct_en: The 〜など〜ていられません + 何か？ combo is Omae's signature: formal verb form plus a dry challenge daring the listener to object.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is casual and chummy — wrong register. (c) apologizes, which is the opposite of Omae's refusal to grant social sympathy.

contrast_examples.en: I can't be bothered to remember things like that. (cold formal)
Sorry, I forgot. (warm casual)

prompt.context_jp: Chiba thanks Omae for intervening with the harasser. Omae denies she was helping.
prompt.prompt_en: Which denial sounds most natural and in-character?

choices.text: 助けてません 私はテイクアウトの客にテイクアウトさせただけです
助けたんじゃないです、ただテイクアウトの人をテイクアウトにしたんです
助けていないと思います、たぶん

feedback.correct_en: The causative 〜させた ('made the customer take it out') produces Omae's deadpan wordplay — crisp and controlled.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) breaks the pun with the odd 'テイクアウトにする' phrasing. (c) softens with たぶん, which contradicts Omae's absolute certainty.

contrast_examples.jp: 客にテイクアウトさせた。
contrast_examples.en: Made the customer take it out. (causative)

contrast_examples.jp: 客をテイクアウトにした。
contrast_examples.en: Turned the customer into take-out. (odd)

prompt.context_jp: At the shrine, Omae prays for the next three months.
prompt.prompt_en: Which wording fits a Japanese shrine prayer best?

choices.text: 何事もなく 平和に過ごせますように
何もなくて 平和に過ごせたらいいです
何事もない 平和な過ごし方を希望します

feedback.correct_en: 〜ますように is the fixed prayer/wish ending — the natural form used when praying at a shrine.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is a casual wish statement, not a prayer. (c) sounds like filling out a request form, not praying.

contrast_examples.en: May I pass the exam. (prayer form)
I hope I pass. (casual wish)

prompt.context_jp: Shoji gets pushy about drinks. Asano shuts him down with a buzzword.
prompt.prompt_en: Which pushback feels most natural for this quick casual moment?

choices.text: 東海林さん それ パワハラ
東海林さん、そのような行為はパワーハラスメントに該当します
東海林さん、それはパワハラだと言えるかもしれません

feedback.correct_en: The clipped noun-ending 'それ パワハラ' is how younger colleagues playfully but pointedly label senior behavior — fast, sharp, no verb needed.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is HR-manual language, way too stiff for a bar. (c) hedges with かもしれません, draining the punch of calling out パワハラ.

contrast_examples.en: That's sexual harassment. (quick callout)

contrast_examples.jp: それはセクハラに該当する可能性があります。
contrast_examples.en: That may constitute sexual harassment. (report-ish)
